<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913940_theRebbe_399" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913940_theRebbe_399__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the drawing down of G-d's kingship on Rosh Hashanah is specifically tied to time and the service of Israel, as the purpose of creation is to make a dwelling for Him in the lower realms, and this is accomplished through the service of Israel, which brings delight.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the explanation of the matter</t>
    <t s="1">(that the drawing down of His kingship, blessed be He, on Rosh Hashanah is specifically connected to a specific time and specifically to the service of Israel),</t>
    <t s="2">is that it is known</t>
    <t s="3">that the ultimate intention of creation is to make for Him, blessed be He, a dwelling place in the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="4">meaning that the revelation of G-dliness below</t>
    <t s="5">(the dwelling place for Him, blessed be He)</t>
    <t s="6">will be specifically within the limitations of the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="7">within the limitations of time and place, and the making of the dwelling place is through Israel.</t>
    <t s="8">And for this reason, the drawing down of the kingship of Rosh Hashanah is specifically within the limitations of time and specifically through the service of Israel.</t>
    <t s="9">And this is what is written,</t>
    <t s="10">"You have affirmed [he'emarta] Hashem today," etc.,</t>
    <t s="11">and the Tzemach Tzedek explains this</t>
    <t s="12">and the Rebbe Maharash</t>
    <t s="13">(in the discourse of this [topic] from the year 1870),</t>
    <t s="14">at the beginning,</t>
    <t s="15">that "he'emarta" has three interpretations,</t>
    <t s="16">and the first interpretation</t>
    <t s="17">(the primary one)</t>
    <t s="18">is "he'emarta" as a term of praise and delight,</t>
    <t s="19">and "today" refers to Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="20">meaning,</t>
    <t s="21">that "you have affirmed today" refers to the drawing down of delight on Rosh Hashanah.</t>
    <t s="22">And as explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="23">that this is also what the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is—the matter of delight,</t>
    <t s="24">shofar from the term "improve [shapru] your deeds."</t>
    <t s="25">From this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="26">that the primary service of Rosh Hashanah is to complete the delight and desire of the Above to make for Him, blessed be He, a dwelling place in the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="27">and this is accomplished through the service of Israel,</t>
    <t s="28">specifically "he'emarta."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses that the building of the kingship on Rosh Hashanah requires removing all concealments and then serving with will, leading to the unification of Havayah and Elokim and the building of Malchus as a partzuf.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it continues afterwards in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="1">that the matter of the building of the kingship—which is on Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="2">as explained in the writings of the AriZal</t>
    <t s="3">—that it is accomplished through the service of "make Me king over you,"</t>
    <t s="4">behold, for this there must be the removal of all concealments and veils, etc.</t>
    <t s="5">And one can explain the continuation of the matters with what was explained previously,</t>
    <t s="6">that since on Rosh Hashanah the kingship is covered and concealed,</t>
    <t s="7">therefore the service of "make Me king over you" is through the prior nullification of the covering, concealment, and veil.</t>
    <t s="8">For this includes the nullification of all matters that cause confusion</t>
    <t s="9">[including the nullification of confusions of the body,</t>
    <t s="10">that there should be a speedy and complete healing, etc.],</t>
    <t s="11">and on the contrary, that it should be in a manner of "double for salvation."</t>
    <t s="12">And behold, after the prior removal of the concealments and veils</t>
    <t s="13">(which is the matter of refinement of the vessel)</t>
    <t s="14">there must be the service with will</t>
    <t s="15">(through which the intensity of the light becomes much greater than the drawing down through refinement of the vessel)</t>
    <t s="16">as explained in the discourse,</t>
    <t s="17">that it can be said that this is the matter of accepting His kingship, blessed be He, in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="18">which is specifically with will,</t>
    <t s="19">and "His kingship</t>
    <t s="20">they accepted upon themselves with will."</t>
    <t s="21">And through the service of nullifying the concealments and veils,</t>
    <t s="22">and the service of "His kingship they accepted upon themselves with will,"</t>
    <t s="23">the building of the kingship is accomplished,</t>
    <t s="24">and even to the perfection of this,</t>
    <t s="25">the unification of Havayah and Elokim,</t>
    <t s="26">the unification of light and flow,</t>
    <t s="27">and even the concealment of the name Elokim</t>
    <t s="28">(the aspect of Malchus)</t>
    <t s="29">itself will shine,</t>
    <t s="30">for this is that the kingship is built in the aspect of a partzuf,</t>
    <t s="31">for the advantage of the aspect of a partzuf of Malchus</t>
    <t s="32">(over the point within it)</t>
    <t s="33">is that it is in the aspect of the revelation of light,</t>
    <t s="34">as explained in the continuation there at length.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the shofar service on Rosh Hashanah involves breaking materiality, which is why it is not done on Shabbat unless in the Temple, where physicality is already perfected and measurement itself is without limit.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it continues there,</t>
    <t s="1">that this is also the explanation of the wording of the blessing of Shofaros,</t>
    <t s="2">"Who hears the sound of the teruah of His people Israel with mercy."</t>
    <t s="3">For teruah is the matter of breaking materiality and selfhood,</t>
    <t s="4">through which one causes the kingship to be in the aspect of the revelation of light.</t>
    <t s="5">Therefore, the festival of Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat</t>
    <t s="6">(as</t>
    <t s="7">(the first day of</t>
    <t s="8">Rosh Hashanah of the determination of this year)</t>
    <t s="9">we do not</t>
    <t s="10">blow [the shofar],</t>
    <t s="11">because on Shabbat the service is not in the manner of breaking and refinement,</t>
    <t s="12">for on Shabbat it is forbidden to separate.</t>
    <t s="13">For the reason for this is that on Shabbat there is the perfection and truth of the matter of physicality,</t>
    <t s="14">and in this there is no need for the service of refinements, etc.</t>
    <t s="15">And it continues,</t>
    <t s="16">"Nevertheless, in the Temple they would blow [the shofar] even on Shabbat,</t>
    <t s="17">because in the Temple, the physical [entity] is in its proper state,</t>
    <t s="18">for it is in the most choice place,</t>
    <t s="19">meaning that the physical is as it should be,</t>
    <t s="20">and therefore in the Temple they would blow [the shofar] even on Shabbat, for this is not a matter of refinement but rather an action of a more elevated perfection in the perfect physical."</t>
    <t s="21">And perhaps one can add to this,</t>
    <t s="22">based on what is known</t>
    <t s="23">that in the Holy of Holies, the place of the Ark is not within measurement,</t>
    <t s="24">meaning that there was in this a matter of measurement and limitation,</t>
    <t s="25">"measuring ten cubits in every direction,"</t>
    <t s="26">and similarly the Ark itself had measurement and limitation,</t>
    <t s="27">"two and a half cubits its length, and a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height,"</t>
    <t s="28">and together with this it is not within measurement,</t>
    <t s="29">because the physical is in its proper state,</t>
    <t s="30">so that the measurement itself is without limit.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
